content: The Birmingham Institute of Art and Design (BIAD) is recognized as the largest British university center for art and design education and research outside of London. It operates as a part of Birmingham City University, which was formerly known as Birmingham Polytechnic and later the University of Central England in Birmingham. The primary campus and library of BIAD are situated at Gosta Green, located just north of Birmingham city center. This location is approximately three-quarters of a mile from both Birmingham New Street railway station and the Custard Factory quarter. Additionally, BIAD maintains smaller centers at various locations. The Bournville center, located in the southern suburbs of the city, offers foundation awards and evening classes. The Margaret Street center, situated in the city center near Birmingham Central Library and Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery, specializes in Fine Art. The Vittoria Street center, located in the city’s Jewelry Quarter, focuses on Jewelry design and education. The International Project Space at Bournville serves as a venue for hosting international art exhibitions and artist residencies. At the Gosta Green campus, BIAD houses the User-lab, a research and design laboratory dedicated to user-centered design methodologies. The Sunday Times University Guide in 2004 rated BIAD’s Art and Design programs as excellent with a score of 5. Birmingham City University has also highlighted that BIAD received an impressive Quality Assurance score of 22 out of 24 for its Art and Design programs, as assessed by the Quality Assurance Agency (QAA). The origins of BIAD can be traced back to the year 1843. It achieved significant development and prominence in the 1890s when it operated as the Birmingham Municipal School of Art at Margaret Street under the leadership of Edward R. Taylor. BIAD’s archives contain extensive records documenting the history of art and design in Birmingham. Additionally, 20 other related collections have been deposited within these archives, further enriching its historical resources.
